title: JSON contracts, made executable in SQL
description: [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) is the de facto contract language for JSON payloads — a declarative way to say what a document must look like. This extension makes those contracts *executable* from inside DuckDB, so a data-quality gate, an ETL contract check, or a default-value fill-in can live in SQL instead of a Pydantic / ajv / jsonschema sidecar. The DuckDB 2.0 build is built on [jsoncons](https://github.com/danielaparker/jsoncons) and supports drafts 4, 6, 7, 2019-09 and 2020-12; the Haybarn 1.5 build uses [pboettch/json-schema-validator](https://github.com/pboettch/json-schema-validator), which targets [draft-07](https://json-schema.org/draft-07/json-schema-release-notes).

sections.title: JSON Schema as an in-SQL contract
sections.description: Validate JSON contracts where the data lives. In the DuckDB 2.0 build, json_schema_is_valid returns TRUE/FALSE and json_schema_errors returns a structured list of failures; json_schema_validate returns TRUE or raises. Schema defaults can also enrich incomplete documents.

bulletPoints.label: Drafts 4 through 2020-12 (DuckDB 2.0 build)
bulletPoints.description: The `$schema` keyword selects [draft 4, 6, 7](https://json-schema.org/specification-links), [2019-09](https://json-schema.org/specification-links#2019-09) or [2020-12](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema) semantics; schemas without `$schema` use 2020-12, and an unknown `$schema` is an error rather than being silently mis-validated. Keywords such as `prefixItems`, `unevaluatedProperties`, `dependentRequired` and `$defs` are enforced. The Haybarn 1.5 build targets draft-07 only.

bulletPoints.label: What the validator covers
bulletPoints.description: Type checks, `required`, `properties` / `patternProperties` / `additionalProperties`, numeric and string bounds, `pattern`, array keywords, combinators (`allOf` / `anyOf` / `oneOf` / `not`, `if` / `then` / `else`), local `$ref`, and `format` assertions (`date-time`, `date`, `email`, `hostname`, `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `uri`, `regex`, …) — in the DuckDB 2.0 build, `format` is validated; the Haybarn 1.5 build raises an error for any schema that uses it.

bulletPoints.label: Schema and data are both JSON
bulletPoints.description: Both the schema and the value under test are passed as DuckDB [`JSON`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/overview) values — a column, a struct literal, or a string cast with `::JSON`. There's no preregistration step, no `ATTACH`, no secret type, and no network: validation runs locally against the in-query schema string.

bulletPoints.label: Default-value enrichment, not just validation
bulletPoints.description: The non-obvious capability: turn the schema's declared `default` values into actual data. One function computes the [JSON Patch (RFC 6902)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6902) diff of `add` operations (useful for an audit log); another applies them inline — taking an incomplete payload to a fully populated record in one expression, with no `COALESCE` cascade.

sections.title: What to know before relying on it
sections.description: The extension is small and focused; it doesn't try to be every JSON-Schema validator out there. Knowing its boundaries keeps it in the role it's good at — a coarse SQL-side gate — rather than where a richer tool belongs.

bulletPoints.label: Errors vs. booleans
bulletPoints.description: `json_schema_validate` returns TRUE on success and raises on failure. In the DuckDB 2.0 build, use `json_schema_is_valid` for a boolean and `json_schema_errors` for a per-keyword report (path, keyword, message); an invalid schema still raises, so a broken contract is never mistaken for bad data. On the Haybarn 1.5 build use COALESCE(TRY(...), false) after checking the schema outside TRY.

bulletPoints.label: No cross-file `$ref` resolution
bulletPoints.description: Each call takes a single `JSON` schema value — there is no filesystem or HTTP `$ref` resolver, so a schema never causes I/O. Inline any `$ref` targets (for example under `$defs`) into the same schema document. References to the standard draft meta-schemas resolve offline.

bulletPoints.label: Safe on untrusted schemas (DuckDB 2.0 build)
bulletPoints.description: `pattern` and `patternProperties` run on [RE2](https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax) — linear time, so a pathological pattern cannot hang or crash the query. RE2 has no lookaround or backreferences; such patterns are reported as schema errors. Schemas and documents nested more than 256 levels are rejected, and deep recursion through `$ref` is stopped with an error before it can exhaust the thread's stack.

bulletPoints.label: Prefer typed columns where you can
bulletPoints.description: If the data has a fixed shape, modeling it as proper DuckDB columns plus [`CHECK` constraints](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/constraints) is cheaper, clearer, and gives better error messages. JSON Schema validation is for the genuinely-JSON case where the shape is contract-defined but the storage stays opaque.

bulletPoints.label: Compiled once per query
bulletPoints.description: In the DuckDB 2.0 build a schema is compiled once per thread and reused for every row (a small cache also covers a schema column with a handful of distinct values), so the per-row cost is the validation itself. For very large tables, validate once on ingest into a staging table rather than re-running the check on every read.
